QASHANI:76:23-25/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:76:23-25/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:76:23-25/r1.claim: God says that He Himself, without another, sent the Qur’an down to the Prophet.
QASHANI:76:23-25/r1.anchor: { إنا نحن نزلنا عليك القرآن } بذاتنا دون من عدانا

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p87/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p87/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p87/r1.claim: The Prophet should persevere despite opponents, trust God, and seek patience through prayer and remembrance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p87/r1.anchor: He will help him in every difficulty.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p87/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p87/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p87/r2.claim: Disbelievers' real ailment is unwillingness to sacrifice immediate gains for the Hereafter; they fabricate objections despite its certainty, though recreating them is easy for God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p87/r2.anchor: The real ailment of the disbelievers is that they do not have the courage to sacrifice the immediate gains of this world

QUSHAYRI:v3p377/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p377/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p377/r12.claim: God sent the Quran down over a period of years.

NAHHAS:v5p106/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p106/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p106/r2.claim: Naḥnu may be accusative adjective of inna's noun, a particle-like separator, or a nominative subject with anzalnā as predicate; tanzīlan is emphatic.
NAHHAS:v5p106/r2.anchor: يكون نحن في موضع نصب صفة لاسم إن ويجوز أن تكون فاصلة لا موضع لها

RAZI-FULL:v30p228#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p228#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p228#2/r5.claim: After the gift of revelation and guidance, the Prophet is told to obey God alone; knowing divine names and attributes is possible, but created minds cannot reach the divine essence.
RAZI-FULL:v30p228#2/r5.anchor: العقول البشرية ليس عندها إلا معرفة الأسماء والصفات

TABATABAI:76:1-22#5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:76:1-22#5/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:76:1-22#5/r4.claim: The commands to be patient and not obey a sinner or unbeliever occur in a later, self-contained section that may have been revealed in Mecca, while the opening section concerning the Prophet's household was Medinan.
TABATABAI:76:1-22#5/r4.anchor: نازلا بمكة، ويؤيده ما في كثير من الروايات المتقدمة إن الذي نزل في أهل البيت بالمدينة هو الفصل الأول

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p345/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p345/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p345/r1.claim: Three emphasis markers in the revelation verse name sender, message, and recipient; greater emphasis is warranted because Quraysh strongly denied revelation but did not deny God as creator, and revelation, the worship-giving book, is creation's purpose.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p345/r1.anchor: فالتوكيد إذن يعتمد على شدة إنكار الشخص للأمر

SAMIN-DURR:76:23/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:76:23/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:76:23/r1.claim: نحن may emphasize the noun of إن, serve as a separating pronoun, or be a subject whose predicate نزلنا forms the predicate clause of إن; in the first two parses, نزلنا itself predicates إن.
SAMIN-DURR:76:23/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يكون " نحن " توكيدا لاسم " إن " ، وأن يكون فصلا و " نزلنا " على هذين الوجهين هو خبر " إن "

SAMIN-DURR:76:23/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:76:23/r2.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:76:23/r2.claim: Makkī analyzes نحن as an accusative adjective of the pronoun in إن, but al-Samīn finds this strange: pronouns are not described by pronouns, and the analysis merely amounts to emphasis.
SAMIN-DURR:76:23/r2.anchor: وقال مكي: " نحن " في موضع نصب على الصفة لاسم " إن " ، لأن المضمر يوصف بالمضمر

ASAD-NOTES:76:23#n21/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:76:23#n21/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:76:23#n21/r1.claim: The verbal form nazzalna implies that Qur'anic revelation came gradually.
ASAD-NOTES:76:23#n21/r1.anchor: The gradualness of Qur'anic revelation is implied in the verbal form nazzalna.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p346/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p346/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p346/r1.claim: He likens the doubled emphasis here to Yā Sīn: the apostles’ stronger rejection after a third messenger is answered with stronger emphasis and the oath ربنا يعلم.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p346/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p346/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p346/r2.claim: The phrase عليك suits the following commands addressed to the Prophet; al-Ḥijr instead centers on the Qur’an and has no surrounding address to him.

QIRAAT-ER:76:23:5#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:76:23:5#1/r1.speaker: hmz
QIRAAT-ER:76:23:5#1/r1.claim: The hmz canonical reading elides hamza in qurʾān to yield Qurān, simplifying the glottal stop without altering meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:76:23:5#1/r1.anchor: Hamza elision: the hamza (ʾ) in qurʾān is dropped, yielding Qurān; canonical reading of some reciters

ALUSI-FULL:v29p150#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p150#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p150#3/r9.claim: Sūrat al-Insān is also called al-Dahr, al-Abrār, al-Amshāj, and Hal Atā. Most authorities cited in al-Baḥr call it Meccan; Mujāhid and Qatāda call it wholly Medinan.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p150#3/r9.anchor: وتسمى سورة الدهر والأبرار والأمشاج وهل أتى وهي مكية عند الجمهور على ما في البحر وقال مجاهد وقتادة مدنية كلها

ALUSI-FULL:v29p150#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p150#3/r10.speaker: الحسن وعكرمة والكلبي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p150#3/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan, ʿIkrima, and al-Kalbī say the sūra is Medinan except for 76:24, which is Meccan; another view makes its closing command to be patient Meccan.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p150#3/r10.anchor: وقال الحسن وعكرمة والكلبي مدنية إلا آية واحدة فمكية وهي ولا تطع منهم آثما أو كفورا وقيل مدنية إلا قوله تعالى فاصبر لحكم ربك إلى آخرها فإنه مكي

ALUSI-FULL:v29p150#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p150#3/r11.speaker: ابن عادل
ALUSI-FULL:v29p150#3/r11.claim: Ibn ʿĀdil records an unrestricted Medinan classification as the majority view, also held by Shīʿa authorities; the sūra has thirty-one verses without disagreement.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p150#3/r11.anchor: وعن ابن عادل حكاية مدنيتها على الإطلاق عن الجمهور وعليه الشيعة وآيها إحدى وثلاثون آية بلا خلاف

ALUSI-FULL:v29p150#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p150#3/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p150#3/r12.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the relationship between this sūra and the preceding one is perfectly clear.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p150#3/r12.anchor: والمناسبة بينها وبين ما قبلها في غاية الوضوح

ALUSI-FULL:v29p165/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p165/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p165/r1.claim: After dividing humanity into obedient and disobedient and describing the abundant mercy prepared for the obedient, God mentions the honor bestowed on the Prophet to ease his loneliness and strengthen his heart.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p165/r1.anchor: ولما ذكرسبحانه أولا حال الإنسان وقسمه إلى الطائع والعاصي وأمعن جل شأنه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p165/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p165/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p165/r2.claim: God sent down the Qurʾān gradually over about twenty-three years for profound reasons that required this mode of revelation; the emphatic pronouns reinforce the assertion.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p165/r2.anchor: أي أنزلناه مفرقا منجما في نحو ثلاث وعشرين سنة لحكم بالغة مقتضية له لا غير

BIQAI-FULL:v8p274/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p274/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p274/r1.claim: The sūra has described guidance, grateful believers and deniers, and their rewards; the pure drink that revives dead earth parallels Qur’anic knowledge reviving dead hearts.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p274/r1.anchor: وختمه بالشراب الطهور الذي من شأنه أن يحيي ميت الأراضي كما أن العلم الذي منبعه القرآن يحيي ميت القلوب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p274/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p274/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p274/r2.claim: The doubled assertion emphasizes God’s limitless greatness and that He alone sent down the Qur’an.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p274/r2.anchor: أي على ما لنا من العظمة التي لا نهاية لها , لا غيرها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p274/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p274/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p274/r3.claim: The Qur’an gathers guidance, guards against deviation, and heals spiritual disorders through the knowledge and practice it teaches.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p274/r3.anchor: الجامع لكل هدى , الحافظ من الزيغ , كما يحفظ الطب للصحيح صحة المزاج , الشافي لما عساه يحصل من الأدواء

BIQAI-FULL:v8p274/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p274/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p274/r4.claim: Tanzīlan denotes gradual revelation governed by wisdom, answering questions and easing people into religious duties step by step.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p274/r4.anchor: أي على التدريج بالحكمة جوابا للسائل ورفقا بالعباد فدرجهم في وظائف الدين تدريجا موافقا للحكمة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p274/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p274/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p274/r5.claim: The added emphasis answers the deniers’ strong rejection and reassures the Prophet’s followers as they patiently await permission to fight.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p274/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p274/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p274/r6.claim: Revelation honors the Prophet in this life before the next; God singled him out in gratitude for his good conduct before prophethood and his avoidance of impurity.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p274/r6.anchor: وخصصناك به شكرا على سيرتك الحسنى التي كانت قبل النبوة , وتجنبك كل ما يدنس

BIQAI-FULL:v8p274/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p274/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p274/r7.claim: Because God revealed it with encompassing knowledge and power, the Qur’an provides comprehensive guidance.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p274/r7.anchor: فلما كان بتنزيلنا كان جامعا للهدى لما لنا من إحاطة العلم والقدرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p440#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p440#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p440#2/r1.claim: God sent down the Quran in separate installments rather than revealing it all at once.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p440#2/r1.anchor: أي فصلناه في الإنزال فلم ننزله جملة واحدة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p674#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p674#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p674#2/r1.claim: Repeating the pronoun after making it the subject doubles emphasis on God’s exclusive role as revealer and assures the Prophet that the staged revelation follows wisdom.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p674#2/r1.anchor: تكرير الضمير بعد إيقاعه إسما لان : تأكيد على تأكيد لمعنى اختصاص الله بالتنزيل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p674#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p674#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p674#2/r2.claim: Only God sent the Qur’an down to the Prophet in stages; as the wise author of every act, He revealed patience and forbearance now and will later command fighting and retribution.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p674#2/r2.anchor: ما نزل عليك القرآن تنزيلا مفرقا منجما إلا أنا لا غيري ، وقد عرفتني حكيما

NASAFI-FULL:v4p302/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p302/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p302/r3.claim: Nasafi classifies Sūrat al-Insān as Meccan and says it has thirty-one verses.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p302/r3.anchor: سورة الانسان مكية وهي احدى وثلاثون آية

NASAFI-FULL:v4p305#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p305#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p305#3/r1.claim: Repeating the pronoun after the named subject adds emphasis upon emphasis.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p305#3/r1.anchor: تكرير الضمير بعد إيقاهم اسما لأن تأكيد على تأكيد

NASAFI-FULL:v4p305#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p305#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p305#3/r2.claim: The construction stresses that Allah alone sends the Qurʾān, reassuring the Prophet that its gradual revelation is wise and purposeful, including the command to persevere.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p305#3/r2.anchor: بمعنى اختصاص الله بالتنزيل ليستقر فين فس النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه إذا كان هو المنزل لم يكن تنزيله مفرقا إلا حكمة وصوابا

RAZI-FULL:v30p225#4/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p225#4/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p225#4/r1.claim: The surah begins by saying humans emerged after nonexistence and were created from mixtures; Razi lists possible mixtures as elements, humors, parental fluids, body and spirit, body and soul, or successive embryonic stages, all pointing to a freely choosing Creator.
RAZI-FULL:v30p225#4/r1.anchor: اعلم أنه سبحانه بين في أول السورة أن الإنسان وجد بعد العدم بقوله : { هل أتى على الإنسان حين من الدهر

RAZI-FULL:v30p225#4/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p225#4/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p225#4/r2.claim: Human beings were not created in vain but for trial and examination.
RAZI-FULL:v30p225#4/r2.anchor: ثم بين بعد ذلك أني ما خلقته ضائعا عاطلا باطلا ، بل خلقته لأجل الابتلاء والامتحان

RAZI-FULL:v30p225#4/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p225#4/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p225#4/r3.claim: God supplied hearing, sight, and reason for the trial, then singled out reason as the noblest faculty and said He guided the path.
RAZI-FULL:v30p225#4/r3.anchor: ثم ذكر تعالى أني أعطيته جميع ما يحتاج إليه عند الابتلاء والامتحان ، وهو السمع والبصر والعقل

RAZI-FULL:v30p225#4/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p225#4/r4.speaker: القدرية
RAZI-FULL:v30p225#4/r4.claim: The division into grateful and ungrateful people is, on the Qadari reading, the result of their own choice.
RAZI-FULL:v30p225#4/r4.anchor: وهذا الإنقسام باختيارهم كما هو تأويل القدرية

RAZI-FULL:v30p225#4/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p225#4/r5.speaker: الجبرية
RAZI-FULL:v30p225#4/r5.claim: The Jabri reading attributes the division into grateful and ungrateful people to God.
RAZI-FULL:v30p225#4/r5.anchor: أو من الله على ما هو تأويل الجبرية

RAZI-FULL:v30p225#4/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p225#4/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p225#4/r6.claim: The surah gives punishment briefly but reward at length; Razi says this signals that mercy is stronger and more prevalent.
RAZI-FULL:v30p225#4/r6.anchor: ذكر عذاب الكفار على الاختصار ، ثم ذكر بعد ذلك ثواب المطيعين على الاستقصاء

RAZI-FULL:v30p225#4/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p225#4/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p225#4/r7.claim: Through “your striving is appreciated,” the surah treats the afterlife; it then shifts to worldly matters and puts the obedient before the rebellious.
RAZI-FULL:v30p225#4/r7.anchor: فظهر مما بينا أن السورة من أولها إلى هذا الموضع في بيان أحوال الآخرة ، ثم إنه تعالى شرع بعد ذلك في أحوال الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v30p225#4/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p225#4/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p225#4/r8.claim: The Messenger is addressed as the head of the obedient community; an introductory reassurance precedes commands and prohibitions to steady him, and prohibitions precede commands because removing harm takes priority over gaining benefit.
RAZI-FULL:v30p225#4/r8.anchor: والرسول هو الرأس والرئيس ، فلهذا خص الرسول بالخطاب . واعلم أن الخطاب إما النهي وإما الأمر

RAZI-FULL:v30p225#4/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p225#4/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p225#4/r9.claim: The surah's arrangement is excellent: its opening subject matter, reassurance, ordering of prohibitions before commands, and later treatment of rebels all fit together.
RAZI-FULL:v30p225#4/r9.anchor: ومن تأمل فيما ذكرناه علم أن هذه السورة ، وقعت على أحسن وجوه الترتيب والنظام

RAZI-FULL:v30p226/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p226/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p226/r1.claim: The verse steadies the Messenger and opens his heart amid accusations of soothsaying and magic: God confirms that the Qur'an is revelation from Him.
RAZI-FULL:v30p226/r1.anchor: واعلم أن المقصود من هذه الآية تثبيت الرسول وشرح صدره فيما نسبوه إليه من كهانة وسحر

RAZI-FULL:v30p226/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p226/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p226/r2.claim: Repeating the pronoun after making it the subject intensifies confirmation: though the unbelievers call it soothsaying, God emphatically declares it true revelation and truthful sending from Him.
RAZI-FULL:v30p226/r2.anchor: فلا جرم بالغ وكرر الضمير بعد إيقاعه اسما ، لأن تأكيدا على تأكيد أبلغ

RAZI-FULL:v30p226/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p226/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p226/r3.claim: The reassurance removes the loneliness caused by the unbelievers' attacks, since the Lord of the heavens honors and confirms the Messenger even if ignorant people slander him.
RAZI-FULL:v30p226/r3.anchor: إحداهما : إزالة الوحشة المتقدمة الحاصلة بسبب طعن أولئك الكفار

RAZI-FULL:v30p226/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p226/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p226/r4.claim: It also strengthens him for future duties: although he wanted to fight those who tormented him, God commands patience and postpones permission to fight according to the wisdom of revelation in stages.
RAZI-FULL:v30p226/r4.anchor: والثانية : تقويته على تحمل التكليف المستقبل ، وذلك لأن الكفار كانوا يبالغون في إيذائه

RAZI-FULL:v30p226/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p226/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p226/r5.claim: The Qur'an was revealed gradually according to wisdom that assigns each matter its appointed time; the Messenger should patiently accept his Lord's wise, faultless decree.
RAZI-FULL:v30p226/r5.anchor: إني ما نزلت عليك هذا القرآن مفرقا منجما إلا لحكمة بالغة تقتضي تخصيص كل شيء بوقت معين

STUDYQURAN:76:23/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:76:23/r1.speaker: JJ, Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:76:23/r1.claim: JJ and Ṭs understand the verse to describe revelation in periodic installments rather than the Quran descending all at once.
STUDYQURAN:76:23/r1.anchor: God revealed the Quran, that is, in periodic installments rather than all at once (JJ, Ṭs).

TAB-FULL:v23p572#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p572#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p572#2/r1.claim: God sent the Qur’an down to Muhammad as a trial and test.
TAB-FULL:v23p572#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {ولا تطع منهم آثما أو كفورا} [الإنسان: 24] قال: نزلت في عدو الله أبي جهل

BURSEVI:v10p213#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p213#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p213#2/r2.claim: God sent the Qurʾān down in successive portions for wise reasons that required gradual revelation.
BURSEVI:v10p213#2/r2.anchor: أي مفرقا منجما لحكم بالغة مقتضية له لا غير

BURSEVI:v10p213#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p213#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p213#2/r3.claim: Repeating the pronoun emphasizes that the Qurʾān is true revelation from the sovereign God, answering Meccan claims that it is sorcery or soothsaying and reassuring the Prophet not to heed their attacks.
BURSEVI:v10p213#2/r3.anchor: فإنا الملك الحق أقول على سبيل التأكيد إن ذلك وحي حق وتنزيل صدق من عندي

ELMALILI:76:23-24/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:76:23-24/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:76:23-24/r1.claim: The doubled “We” stresses that God alone revealed the Qur’an to the Prophet.
ELMALILI:76:23-24/r1.anchor: Başkası değil Biz, ancak Biz indirdik sana {ٱلْقُرْءَانَ} Kur’ân’ı

ELMALILI:76:23-24/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:76:23-24/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:76:23-24/r2.claim: Elmalılı describes the Qur’an as guiding humanity to the right path and offering the delight of the pure drink.
ELMALILI:76:23-24/r2.anchor: Kur’ân’ı insana doğru yolu gösteren ve o şarâb-ı tahûr neş’esini sunan Kur’ân’ı

ELMALILI:76:23-24/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:76:23-24/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:76:23-24/r3.claim: The Qur’an came in installments over twenty-three years, not all at once; its gradual development parallels the stages of the first human’s creation.
ELMALILI:76:23-24/r3.anchor: bir defada değil, zaman zaman fâsıla ile yirmi üç senede ceste ceste, ki ilk insan hilkatinde olduğu gibi bunda da tedrîcî tekemmül ve terakki kāidesine bir uygunluk vardır

ELMALILI:76:23-24/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:76:23-24/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:76:23-24/r4.claim: This revelation will bring about many things not previously mentioned, and the promised events will certainly occur.
ELMALILI:76:23-24/r4.anchor: Bununla önceden mezkur olmayan birçok şeyler olacak ve bu vaad olunan şeyler muhakkak vukū‘bulacaktır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:23/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:23/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:23/r1.claim: The preceding verses describe the afterlife outcomes people reach according to the value of their worldly beliefs and deeds.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:23/r1.anchor: Allah Teâlâ önceki âyetlerde insanların dünyadaki inanç ve eylemlerinin değerine göre âhirette ulaşacakları sonuçları tasvir etmişti.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:23/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:23/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:23/r2.claim: These verses remind the Prophet of revelation’s value and urge him to remain steadfast in worship and carrying out God’s commands, strengthening his resolve against the deniers.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:23/r2.anchor: Bu âyetler ise Hz. Peygamber’e vahyin değerini hatırlatıyor; Allah’ın hükümlerini yerine getirmede kararlı olup ibadet etmesini öğütlüyor.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p347/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p347/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p347/r1.claim: The surah names the revelation Quran only here; using dhikr in al-Hijr answers Quraysh's own label and better fits the preceding verse.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p347/r1.anchor: فلما سماه كفار قريش ذكراً ردّ عليهم الله تعالى بكلمة (الذكر) ولهذا فهي أنسب للآية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p298#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p298#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p298#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Quran was sent down in separate verses, not all at once.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p298#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: 182/أمتفرقا آية بعد آية،

BAYDAWI-FULL:76:22-24/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:76:22-24/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:76:22-24/r3.claim: The Qurʾān was sent down in stages for a wisdom that required gradual revelation.

BAYDAWI-FULL:76:22-24/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:76:22-24/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:76:22-24/r4.claim: Repeating the pronoun with inna emphasizes that the revelation is specifically God's act.
BAYDAWI-FULL:76:22-24/r4.anchor: وتكرير الضمير مع أن مزيد لاختصاص التنزيل به

MUQATIL:76:23-24/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:76:23-24/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:76:23-24/r1.claim: Muqatil returns to the earlier command that Muhammad be patient with God's judgment.
MUQATIL:76:23-24/r1.anchor: ثم رجع إلى قوله عز وجل الأول: { إنا نحن نزلنا عليك القرآن تنزيلا فاصبر لحكم ربك

QURTUBI-FULL:76:23-24/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:23-24/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:76:23-24/r1.claim: The Qur’an is truly sent down by God; the Prophet did not invent it or produce it on his own, despite the polytheists’ claim.
QURTUBI-FULL:76:23-24/r1.anchor: ما افتريته ولا جئت به من عندك، ولا من تلقاء نفسك

QURTUBI-FULL:76:23-24/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:23-24/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:76:23-24/r2.claim: After the prior promises and threats, the verse establishes that the book contains what people need and is truth, not magic, soothsaying or poetry.
QURTUBI-FULL:76:23-24/r2.anchor: لما ذكر أصناف الوعد والوعيد، بين أن هذا الكتاب يتضمن ما بالناس حاجة إليه

QURTUBI-FULL:76:23-24/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:23-24/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:76:23-24/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Qur’an came in portions, verse after verse, not all at once, explaining nazalnā.
QURTUBI-FULL:76:23-24/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: أنزل القرآن متفرقا: آية بعد آية
